id: An Audience with Sir Tony Robinson-The Opera House, Wellington, New Zealand-Wellington NZ
name: An Audience with Sir Tony Robinson
venue: The Opera House, Wellington, New Zealand
long_description:
After a sold-out tour in early 2026, Sir Tony Robinson brings his talk show back to Wellington. Catch ‘An Audience with Sir Tony Robinson’ at The Opera House. The television presenter, actor, and award-winning writer has an impressive decades-long career. Tony will divulge behind-the-scenes stories from his life on and off screen. He’ll then read from his fiction debut ‘The House of Wolf’, an epic tale of Alfred the Great and the bloody birth of England. He won’t hog the microphone the whole time — you’ll also get the chance to ask him questions. Expect masterful storytelling from Tony and lots of laughs from the audience. 

You might have seen Tony play Baldrick in Rowan Atkinson’s cult 80s sitcom ‘Blackadder’. In the show, his “I have a cunning plan” catchphrase and comedic timing made him a household name. He’s also celebrated for his work in historical broadcasting, which includes presenting 20 seasons of ‘Time Team’. His infectious enthusiasm for history continued, as he wrote his first novel aged 78. The book delves into the (often grim) realities of life for ordinary people caught between Saxon kings and Viking raiders.

id: Air Force in Concert with Bret McKenzie-Michael Fowler Centre, Wellington, New Zealand-Wellington NZ
name: Air Force in Concert with Bret McKenzie
venue: Michael Fowler Centre, Wellington, New Zealand
long_description:
Join two major Wellington talents for an afternoon of musical delights. The Michael Fowler Centre hosts a collaborative show for the whole family. ‘Air Force in Concert with Bret McKenzie’ includes kid-friendly hits from Flight of the Conchords, The Muppets, The Black Seeds, and Brett's recent album. The band plays tunes ranging from symphonic favourites and toe-tapping marches to movie classics and pop hits. There’s a rumour that a sousaphone will be one of the instruments that makes an appearance. Expect laughs, expect brass, expect philosophical lyrics like “life’s a fillet of fish”. 

Bret is best known as one half of the internationally celebrated comedy duo Flight of the Conchords. He formed it with Jemaine Clement in 1998. Since then, he’s become a Grammy and Academy Award-winning songwriter and performer. Known for crafting witty and wonderful songs. The Royal New Zealand Air Force Band is a reserve force military band based in Wellington. They perform regularly to welcome dignitaries at the Government House and Parliament. They also provide music for parades and commemorations at Pukeahu National War Memorial.

id: Chopper — Gold-The Opera House, Wellington, New Zealand-Wellington NZ
name: Chopper — Gold
venue: The Opera House, Wellington, New Zealand
long_description:
Buckle up, Wellington — Chopper is back and not mincing words. The Australian comedian, otherwise known as Heath Franklin, is storming The Opera House with his new show ‘Chopper - Gold’. As usual, his take-no-prisoners sense of humour will be on display. For his 2026 tour, he’s delivering two decades of his funniest gags. Revisit sketches from The Ronnie Johns Half Hour: a comedy show Heath made with his uni mates. Expect a big dose of swearing with big hits like Harden the F*** Up, The Weather sketch, and Shopping at Bunnings. 

While Chopper has his tongue firmly in his cheek, the audience will be clutching at pearls in horror or clutching their sides in fits of laughter. When Chopper is not shocking crowds, he’s appearing on New Zealand television show ‘7 Days’. He also has a string of Australian television appearances.

id: The Beatles Anthology-The Opera House, Wellington, New Zealand-Wellington NZ
name: The Beatles Anthology
venue: The Opera House, Wellington, New Zealand
long_description:
Tribute band The Beatles Anthology is coming to The Opera House in June. For two hours, the show will take you down the long and winding road of The Beatles’ greatest hits. Expect the band to cover the era of matching suits and mop haircuts to the later experimental days. The four singers stand out for their authenticity and attention to detail, bringing the essence of The Beatles to life in every show. 

You might hear classics like Let It Be, Lucy in the Sky with Diamonds, and Yellow Submarine. Often regarded as the most influential band in popular music, The Beatles need little introduction. The Beatles Anthology brings a performance that captures the spirit of the Fab Four to Wellington audiences. This concert has the costumes, the hairstyles, the banter, and the gear. It’s not The Beatles, but it’ll feel like it.

id: Miss Saigon-Michael Fowler Centre, Wellington, New Zealand-Wellington NZ
name: Miss Saigon
venue: Michael Fowler Centre, Wellington, New Zealand
long_description:
Tragic pop-musical Miss Saigon hasn’t played Wellington in over 15 years. Fabulous soloists, a 40-strong local choir, and a live orchestra are rectifying that in 2027. G&T Productions brings a semi-staged concert to the Michael Fowler Centre. This format puts the performers and music front and centre. Set during the final days of the Vietnam War in 1975, Miss Saigon is a heartbreaking, bold, and gripping musical theatre piece. 

From the songwriting team behind ‘Les Misérables’, Miss Saigon is a tragic love story of a young Vietnamese woman (Kim) who falls in love with an American soldier (Chris). Saigon falls, and their story unfolds alongside the Engineer, a ruthless survivor chasing his own ‘American Dream’. 

Wellingtonian Maya Handa Naff plays Kim. She has previously sung the role in the United States. Maya is an actor, director, and teacher whose Wellington performance credits include ‘Wicked’ (Glinda) and ‘Les Misérables’ (Eponine). Director and actor Kyle Chuen plays Chris. Laurence Mossman returns as Thuy after performing the part on Australian and international tours. Expect to hear songs like I’d Give My Life for You, Why God Why, and Bui Doi.
